issues.description: The problem statement and UML require messageOnMilk() to return a String (e.g., "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), but the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a boolean and the implementations print the milking message internally and return true. The template's Main prints the return value of messageOnMilk(), which implies a printable message (String). This mismatch between the specification (String) and the solution (boolean) is structural and will confuse students about the correct return type and how to implement the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem specification: change Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String and have implementations return the milking message (e.g., "Goat Buttinsky is milked") instead of printing it internally and returning a boolean. Update implementations (Seal, Goat) to return the String and remove internal System.out.println from the method. Keep Main (and any callers) printing the returned String. This preserves the intended design and the UML/text description.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML require Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return a String containing the milk message (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") and the example Main() prints that returned String. However, the solution defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() with a boolean return type and the Seal/Goat implementations print the message to the console and return true. This mismatch in the method's signature/behavior (expected String vs. implemented boolean) creates a conceptual/API inconsistency that will confuse students about the expected return type and usage of messageOnMilk().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Milkable API with the problem statement: change the interface signature to public String messageOnMilk(); and update Seal and Goat to return the message string (e.g. return "Seal " + getName() + " is milked";) instead of printing and returning a boolean. This preserves the expected usage where callers print the returned String.
